title: OpenAI Saudi national bugging case shows threat to U.S. leadership in AI: DNI Clayton
source_used: CNBC interview, as relayed by Stocktwits on TradingView (CNBC page returned HTTP 403)
key_facts: White House Super Intelligence Force Chair Jay Clayton spoke to CNBC on Friday after the force's first meeting in Washington, D.C.
He said both commercial espionage and state-sponsored espionage are realities.
He cited the OpenAI bugging case as evidence of the lengths people will go to try to supplant US leadership, but did not say the OpenAI case itself was state-sponsored.

The FBI earlier this month charged a 35-year-old Saudi national and OpenAI employee with allegedly installing a covert audio-recording device in an executive conference room at OpenAI's San Francisco offices.
The Justice Department says the device was plugged into a USB port behind a television and concealed in toilet paper.
Clayton said the US is competing not only with China but also with Russia, Iran and North Korea, which he said have significant AI capabilities.
The force set up workstreams on AI risks and accountability, including a risk study by the President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology led by David Sacks.
quote_evidence: “Both commercial espionage and, I would say, state-sponsored espionage are realities,” he said in an interview with CNBC after the force’s first meeting.
He cited the OpenAI bugging case as evidence of “the lengths that people will go to try and supplant our leadership.” However, he did not say the OpenAI case itself was state-sponsored.
According to the Justice Department, the device was found plugged into a USB port behind a television and was concealed in toilet paper.
why_it_matters_hint: A senior White House official links the OpenAI bugging case to a wider espionage threat to US AI leadership, without saying a state was behind it.
notes: CNBC page blocked (HTTP 403); text read in a Stocktwits article on TradingView that reports the CNBC interview. Title conflict: the CNBC headline calls Clayton 'DNI'; Stocktwits calls him White House Super Intelligence Force Chair, and the entry uses the latter because the text supports it. The accused is not named in the entry.
